I took a huge leap by moving to Hungary from the USA after my ex-girlfriend racked up huge debt on my credit cards. I went with only 100USD to my name after buying plane tickets and renting a hotel, but knowing that I would get a few thousand coming in the bank 2 months later. I managed to hustle to make money to eat when I ran out of money and in the interim I lived off the mini bar in the hotel. I made connections with family I had never met before and they helped me get on my feet while I waited for my money to come into my account. I then found out that I had citizenship in the country, because my mother had arranged it for me when I was a child (I could claim this as my mother is Hungarian). I almost went broke trying to find a job after getting a flat and not making enough money hosting on airbnb with my spare room. I had to borrow money from a girl I had only known for a few months, and have only managed to pay her back half - as I'm trying to pay my outstanding debt... I left a few accounts go to collections but I had to pay off the other two as they are linked to bank accounts I still use. That being said I have a job now and my life is tremendously better than it was before. Despite my debts I live in a much bigger flat and eat out more often and generally enjoy life much more due to a cheaper standard of living in Hungary (I also should mention i barely speak the language). I highly recommend taking a calculated risk like I did. I knew I could connect with family, but I had no idea that I would get as much support as they gave me. My life is on an upward track and I could have been totally devastated by the insane decision I made to move to a foreign country with no game plan. I truly believe that fortune favors the bold. Do something that inspires you. I felt it in my bones that I was making the right decision and things always turned out okay even when the outlook was grim.

I think getting citizenship in other countries is much more difficult than you might expect. Generally, you need to be able to prove that you have money in order to go legally. I'd focus first on getting your credit situation straightened out with your mom. The longer you wait, the more difficult it's going to be.
